statement: For the same Chrome version, curl_cffi and httpcloak sent identical JA4 and peetprint fingerprints in the live test.
httpcloak's chrome-latest-windows preset matched the real Chrome 157 on this machine on both JA4 and peetprint.
curl_cffi 0.16.3, the version log runs, stops at chrome150 and its Chrome targets carry a macOS user agent.
curl_cffi 0.17.0 adds Windows Chrome targets (chrome151, chrome152) and Windows Firefox 153-155.
httpcloak's documentation shows no WebSocket client API.
httpcloak's documentation shows no asyncio API for Python.
curl_cffi WebSocket handshakes use the same impersonated TLS fingerprint, proxies and cookies as its HTTP requests.
JWriter20, the Camoufox maintainer, recommended httpcloak in Scraping Enthusiasts.
Scraping Enthusiasts members reported that random JA3 fingerprints still get blocked and recommended copying a real browser.
A member reported that a platform ties cookies to the JA3/JA4 fingerprint they were issued to.
log's HTTP clients today present more than three different browser identities.
Both libraries produced the same Akamai HTTP/2 fingerprint as real Chrome in the live test.
